correctness.rationale: For any binary factor with at most k ones, k tortoise passes fully sort it. Thue–Morse complementary pairs force this for lengths below 2k and force every exceptional weight-(k+1) factor at length 2k to end in one, so it too sorts. At length 2k+1 only weights k and k+1 occur; a weight-(k+1) factor ends in either one or exactly one trailing zero, giving exactly two distinct high-weight outputs. The digit-sum witness i=2^r-k with r congruent to s_2(k-1) modulo two realizes both high outputs; a low-weight factor realizes the third. All quantifiers and the empty factor are covered. Direct map versus closed form was checked on 49,150 word/iterate cases, and complete morphic factor sets were checked for k<=128; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The leading 2026 paper explicitly introduces the Abelian-agreement length and invites evaluation for the Thue–Morse word; inspection of its relevant full text did not reveal the all-iterate answer. Two highly relevant published results with two iterations address long-length deficit formulas and maximum fibers, neither the first-disagreement invariant at all iteration counts. Four implication-based checks and the accessible own-ledger claim comparison found no equivalent or stronger statement. Elementary derivability and any unindexed equivalent remain explicit residual risks.

value.rationale: The 2026 introductory paper isolates Abelian-agreement depth as a natural statistic of repeated partial sorting and expressly invites studying it for Thue–Morse. This theorem completely determines that exact function for every positive iteration count and identifies the first failure with a three-image classification and explicit witnesses. The numerical cutoff measures how many iterations are sufficient to erase positional information from all factors up to a given length; it is not an arbitrary finite slice or a restatement of the one-step formula.
